title: Multimodal learned features classify prostate lymph-node involvement
summary: A stacked model combined pretrained MRI image features, radiomics and clinical information to classify pathology-referenced pelvic lymph-node involvement. Its AUC was 0.92 in 71 internal test patients and0.76 in 50 second-center patients. This retrospective validation does not establish avoided surgery or routine clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Pretrained image-network embeddings; random-forest signatures; AutoGluon stacked ensemble

evidence.tested: 401 selected surgical patients:280 development,71 internal test and50 second-center test. Only six second-center patients had positive nodes; sensitivity there was50% at the development-selected threshold.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective surgical selection, small external positive count and site-specific readers limit transfer. Tumor segmentation used radiological-pathological correlation; preprocessing and feature-selection isolation are not completely specified. Source feature-importance description contains unrelated linker terminology. Surgery avoidance and decision-curve benefits are hypothetical.
evidence.ai_role: ImageNet-pretrained networks embed tumor/peritumoral MRI regions; forests select/learn imaging signatures and an ensemble integrates them with clinical and reader variables.

source_review.scope: Actual primary clinical/model Methods2.1–2.8, diagnostic Results3.2 and limitations; fresh exact PubMed date/notice metadata. No independent implementation or supplementary detail reproduction.
